mission: The largest philanthropic funder of AI safety. Its 'Navigating Transformative AI' fund (570+ grants) supports technical AI safety, AI governance and policy, capacity building, and new projects suited to short timelines; Good Ventures is the main partner. Status: Open Philanthropy rebranded as Coefficient Giving in late 2025. The site says Coefficient 'has directed over $7 billion in grants since 2014' across all causes.

key_work.title: Our Approach to AI Safety and Security
key_work.plain_summary: Explains its three pillars: visibility into AI capabilities (evals, forecasting), technical and policy safeguards against catastrophe, and growing the talent pipeline.

key_work.title: We're Urgently Scaling Our Work on AI and Biosecurity
key_work.plain_summary: Says transformative AI 'may arrive soon, and the world isn't ready', so it is giving more, deciding faster and urging grantees to raise ambitions.

key_work.title: Project Tailwind: a call for founders
key_work.plain_summary: Recruits founders to launch new institutions addressing catastrophic AI risk, with a published list of priority projects.

key_work.title: RFP: Capacity building for transformative AI risks
key_work.plain_summary: Open call funding projects that help new talent move into AI safety, support existing talent and improve public discussion.

funding_note: Primary funding from Good Ventures (Dustin Moskovitz & Cari Tuna).
events: Open Philanthropy rebrands as Coefficient Giving

people.role: Co-founder of Open Philanthropy (now at Anthropic)

warnings.text: There is 'a strong possibility that AI systems will soon outperform humans in nearly all cognitive domains' (Navigating Transformative AI fund page).
AI-related misuse, loss of control or drastic societal change could endanger human civilisation.
Transformative AI may arrive soon and the world isn't ready (2026 blog).

recommendations.text: Fund technical research to make AI 'more trustworthy, robust, controllable, and aligned'.
Fund AI governance and policy for safe, secure, responsibly managed development.
Grow the field via capacity building and career-transition funding, and launch new organisations (Project Tailwind).
